anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L1 Simplified reference is a 5x5x3 depth-sorted voxel pile with four target diamonds, a visible lava hazard, and one fragile support. Its mining changes occlusion, but the task is a fixed pile of raycast clicks and rotations. Crater Walker d1 has one state-changing leg transfer: the agent must infer a 3D foothold, preserve three contacts and posture, and drive signed yaw/lift/extend controls before the body transit. That makes Crater Walker d1 more stateful and motor-spatial than this L1 reference despite having fewer target objects.

evidence.explanation: The approved Mine baseline is L1 Simplified and its baseline risk/target configuration is explicit.
The Mine generator constructs target/blocker/cap voxels, optional hazards/support, and a deterministic sequence of ray-solvable mining steps.
The Mine UI rotates a view and mines by canvas raycast clicks, with material-specific outcomes.
The Mine grader replays rotations, click-ray occlusion, durability, mining outcomes, and support collapse.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L2 Full reference is one active-vision field: cursor position causes a hidden constellation to converge while two false convergence points and noise stars compete for attention, followed by one accepted-radius click. It has no persistent body/support ledger after the click. Crater Walker d1 already couples a release, a precise 3D placement, support safety, and body movement; d2 adds a second such dependency and a decoy. The Crater profiles therefore sit above or around this L2 reference rather than treating one transfer as L1.

evidence.explanation: The approved Constellation baseline is L2 Full with active cursor reveal, decoys, noise, and a 28-pixel accepted center.
The anchor generator creates a moving/revealing 112-star field with false convergence points and a final expected click.
The Full anchor uses canvas pointer motion/click; the alternate surface uses coordinate controls, with no multi-stage world state.
The anchor grader checks only the accepted click location and the selected input source.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L3 Full reference continuously integrates tilt physics while the ball crosses three ordered lamps, three walls, and three wells, with a minimum tick/control requirement. Crater Walker d3 has three dependent support transfers and two decoys, but its four-step body paths are action-gated and the next leg is explicitly highlighted; it has more 3D contact/posture precision but less continuous steering and less autonomous temporal pressure. This makes d3 a plausible high-L3 comparison, while d4's extra transfer, decoy, and tighter support/posture envelope support moving it into the approved L4 band without claiming that every burden dominates Gyro.

evidence.explanation: The approved Gyro baseline is L3 Full with three ordered lamps, three walls, three wells, and live analog tilt.
The anchor generator materializes the ordered physics course and deterministic replay contract.
The anchor browser advances autonomous physics ticks from continuous tilt and handles collisions, hazards, ordered goals, and the cup.
The anchor grader replays physics ticks, input source, hazards, ordered lamps, and minimum activity requirements.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L4 Full reference is an 18x11 warehouse with five face gates, a 48-to-105-roll route contract, and only four sparse orientation scanners; every move changes die orientation and future gate feasibility. Crater Walker d4 has four support transfers, three actuator channels per transfer, posture and terrain checks, and four body-transit settles per landing. Crater exposes the pads and next transfer leg, so it carries less hidden orientation/path-memory burden than Blind Dice, but it carries comparable multi-step state and 3D motor precision. This is a close L4 reference rather than evidence for L5.

evidence.explanation: The approved Dice baseline is L4 Full with five barriers/gates, sparse scanners, and a 48-to-105-roll route.

The anchor grader replays each roll, orientation, gate, scanner/path ledger, and input source.

anchor_comparisons.concrete_comparison: The approved L5 Simplified reference requires four valid adjacent swaps on a 5x5 board to reach an exact score. Each valid swap changes the board through gravity/refill and cascade waves; a black licorice position voids the receipt. Crater Walker d5 adds a fifth state-dependent support transfer and five decoys with a .25 contact tolerance, but its visible pads, transfer marker, and deterministic actuator geometry make the route much less combinatorial than Exact-Change's changing-board exact-score search. D5 is therefore a high-L4 candidate, not a source-supported L5 reassignment.

visible_baseline_solution: From screenshots, read the task prompt, the 3D crater canvas, the gold contact pads, the blue available pads, the gray decoys, the current support count, posture readout, terrace number, and highlighted TRANSFER LEG card. Use the visible view buttons (and the currently shared canvas orbit gesture) to separate near and far ledges. For the indicated leg only, use the Simplified card's signed YAW, LIFT, and EXTEND +/- controls. Raise its LIFT to the release threshold 3 and press SETTLE while the other three feet remain on their current pads. Set YAW and EXTEND from the relative 3D location of the next real ledge, lower LIFT onto that ledge, and press SETTLE again. After a valid landing, press SETTLE through the four visible body-transit poses; remember the new terrace, contacts, and newly highlighted leg. Repeat for all four transfers, maintaining at least three contacts and posture within the displayed rule. When the body reaches the outside ledge with four contacts, press CERTIFY ESCAPE. A failed settle ends the instance; NEW ATTEMPT requests a fresh challenge rather than undoing the failed state.

baseline_judgment.rationale: The explicit baseline is d4 Simplified, and the source supports retaining that approved-style L4 placement provisionally. The screenshot-only task requires active 3D spatial interpretation, integer actuator precision, support/posture reasoning, memory of released/current contacts, and a sequence of state-changing transfers. D4 has five terraces/four transfers, three active decoys, .30 contact tolerance, .36 posture limit, and a three-channel foot placement problem. It is materially above the approved L1 Mine and L2 Constellation references, comparable in multi-step state to approved L4 Blind Dice Courier but with less hidden route/orientation memory, and below approved L5 Exact-Change Candy Cascade's changing-board exact-score planning. D3 remains a plausible high-L3 comparison because Crater's body transit is button-gated and the next transfer is explicitly marked; d4's additional transfer, decoy, and tighter contact/posture conditions support the current L4 label.

Controls change signed actuator values; SETTLE enforces three-point support/posture, release/landing order, and four-step body transit.

uncertainties: No human or computer-use-agent completion-rate, time, or usability calibration is present; the task metadata explicitly says calibration is pending.
The absolute boundary between d3 and approved L3 Gyroscopic Tilt Board, and the amount of motor precision versus hidden memory in L4 references, remains source-based rather than measured.

adjacent_pairs.simplified_change: The same world transition is performed through +/- nudges: stage_count 2->3 adds a second state-changing support transfer/body pose; decoy_count 0->1 adds a real gray contact candidate; tolerance .48->.42, elevation .32->.40, lateral .06->.11, terrain detail 3->4, and posture limit .48->.44 narrow/alter the visible and contact problem.
adjacent_pairs.full_change: The same added terrace, dependent body/support state, decoy, and geometry/tolerance changes apply while actuator values are set with direct rails. No timing or physics parameter is changed by the interaction mode.
adjacent_pairs.ordering_assessment: Supported relative increase. The new terrace is not merely an independent repetition: a valid first landing changes body pose, current support ledger, and the next indicated leg before the second transfer. The fixed four body-path steps and 240 ms settle tick are held constant and are not credited as difficulty.

adjacent_pairs.full_change: The same third-transfer, decoy, and active geometry/posture changes apply with direct actuator rails. The logical actuator effects and SETTLE transition remain unchanged.

findings.claim: Simplified mode also accepts direct canvas dragging for orbit, so the camera input surface is not exclusive to Full.
findings.causal_explanation: The controls contract describes Simplified orbit through visible view buttons and Full orbit through viewport dragging, but the Crater browser installs pointerdown/pointermove handlers on the canvas without a mode guard. This lets a Simplified user orbit by drag as well as by buttons. The camera is explicitly view-only, and the grader records/replays actuator and SETTLE events rather than camera events, so the leak does not change world state, success, or cross-mode actuator acceptance and does not justify a difficulty relabel.

evidence.explanation: The declared Simplified and Full interaction summaries distinguish view buttons from viewport dragging.
The browser selects the actuator surface by mode but installs the canvas orbit handlers unconditionally.
The world rules state that camera motion changes only the view, not the world or success condition.
The grader validates control/settle event sources and state replay; it has no camera-event path.

findings.recommended_action: If interaction contracts require exclusive input surfaces, gate the canvas pointer handlers on Full or document orbit as a shared affordance. The parent should visually verify that button-based Simplified orbit provides equivalent task-relevant views.

concise_summary: Keep the current L4 Simplified baseline. Source evidence supports a distinguished, monotonic five-profile ladder: higher profiles add state-changing support transfers plus active decoy, precision, elevation, terrain, and posture demands. The absolute profile placements are hypotheses, not human or agent calibration results; no runtime checks were run.
limitations: This is a source-only audit; runtime generation, browser, grading, export, VNC, human, and agent checks were not run.
Historical pre-controls preservation cannot be established from the supplied source.
The public serialized world contains implementation state needed by the browser, but page-state/DOM inspection is forbidden by the task and is excluded from the screenshot-only assessment.
